text: Continuous integration, or CI, is a practice where developers regularly add their code to a shared project. Every time someone makes a change, automated builds start immediately. The system then runs tests to check that the new code works correctly with the rest of the project. This helps teams catch issues early, before they become serious problems. CI pipelines organise these steps into a clear process, so every change goes through the same checks. As a result, teams can find bugs faster and release software more reliably.
